nodes.title: Galatians: No Other Gospel
nodes.summary: Paul's angriest letter — no thanksgiving, straight to 'I am astonished': teachers are requiring circumcision, and Paul treats it as a different gospel entirely. Abraham believed before the law existed; the law was a guardian until Christ; 'there is neither Jew nor Greek… for you are all one in Christ Jesus.' Freedom lands in the Spirit's fruit — love, joy, peace — against the flesh's works.

prerequisites.reason: Galatians 3's whole case is Abraham's faith-before-circumcision and the promise to his 'seed.'
The circumcision crisis is the letter's occasion — Acts 15 narrates the same fight from the outside.
'Cursed is everyone hanged on a tree' and the law's curse come from Deuteronomy 21 and 27.

connections.reason: Romans is Galatians' argument rewritten at full length and lower temperature.
'The righteous shall live by faith' does its work here as in Romans.

nodes.discussion_prompt: Paul writes with real heat because he believes the gospel itself is at stake. Why does adding requirements to grace change the message entirely, and where are you tempted to treat God's acceptance as something you have to earn?
assessment_questions: What are the teachers in Galatia requiring of Gentile believers, and how does Paul describe their message in chapter 1?
Paul points to Abraham, who believed God long before the law was given. How does Abraham's story support Paul's case about how people are made right with God?
Paul says freedom in Christ is given for serving one another in love. Where could you use your freedom to serve someone this week, and what would it cost you?

teaching_concepts.explanation: Paul treats a message of Christ plus added requirements as a different gospel altogether, because it shifts the ground of salvation away from grace.
Right standing with God comes through trusting Christ, since no one can earn it by works of the law.
The law served as a guardian until Christ came, pointing forward to the faith and full sonship now given in him.
Christian freedom exists for love and the Spirit's fruit, so it looks like serving others rather than gratifying the flesh.

nodes.completion_criteria: Explain in your own words why Paul insists there is no other gospel, and describe how the fruit of the Spirit shows what real freedom looks like.

comprehension_check.question: Paul calls the Galatian teaching a different gospel, though it kept Christ and added only circumcision. Why does the addition change everything?
options: Because a required addition moves the ground off Christ's work
Because the demand burdened converts Paul hoped to win more easily
Because the teachers lacked authorization from the apostles in Jerusalem
comprehension_check.why: Galatians 2:16 states the ground of justification, faith in Christ rather than works of law, which the added requirement overturns.
comprehension_check.hint: Read Galatians 1:6-9 and 2:16 again. Notice what Paul says is actually at stake in the addition.

comprehension_check.question: Galatians 5 announces freedom from the law and immediately warns against misusing it. What is the freedom for?
options: For each conscience to set its own standard of conduct
For enjoying what the law once denied, within sensible limits
For serving one another in love, walking by the Spirit
For proving to its critics that grace produces better conduct
comprehension_check.why: Galatians 5:13 turns freedom outward, a calling exercised in love and service toward one another.
comprehension_check.hint: Read Galatians 5:13-14 and 5:22-23 again. Notice what freedom produces when the Spirit is leading it.
